items.note: Experiment comparing human-only, human-AI collaboration, and AI-only design of CSR initiatives, with expert and GenAI ratings of quality, novelty, and feasibility; conference abstract only, sample size and assignment not stated.

System paper (Creative Blends, LLM plus text-to-image for visual blends) with a 24-person user study reporting more creative blend ideation; whether there is a baseline condition is not stated; same work as arXiv 2502.16062; below 50 participants.

Study 2 has people generate ideas with a culturally aligned versus misaligned LLM (ChatGPT, ErnieBot) and scores usefulness and novelty; Study 1 is model-only and Study 3 uses field data; conference abstract, sample size not stated.

52 novices design products with a text-to-image tool using the DesignWeaver scaffolding interface, reported as producing more diverse and innovative designs; the abstract does not name the comparison condition (the search notes say a baseline interface); same work as arXiv 2502.09867.

Randomized LLM feedback on over 20,000 ICLR 2025 peer reviews; outcomes are review updating, length, informativeness, and rebuttal engagement, with no creativity or diversity outcome and not a creative task.

Mixed-method classroom experiments with AI-supported ideation in industrial and UI design courses plus surveys; reports enhanced creativity, but the comparison condition, sample size, and whether creativity is scored on outputs are not stated.

Participants list features of concepts in a standard task versus a variant with bandit-chosen algorithmic hints (fluency outcome), with GPT-4 run as a simulated participant; check in full text whether the hints come from generative AI, because if not it is out as not_generative_ai.

Design-engineering participants solve conceptual design challenges with GPT-4 without explanations (n=39) or an explainable-AI LLM framework (n=39), and 10 separate raters score usefulness, feasibility, originality, and credibility; an ai_design contrast; the abstract's 88 includes the raters.

Compares improvised 'Yes! and' stories that people co-create with an LLM agent versus with a human partner, rated for novelty, value, and surprise (no difference); abstract from the ICCC 2025 program page, which states no sample size or design, so the comparison may be AI-vs-human output rather than an assistance experiment.

Between-subjects study with 46 participants on 2D structural design tasks comparing a high-fidelity and a low-fidelity reflective AI agent with a no-AI control; outcomes are design objectives, solution quality, and design-space exploration rather than rated creativity; below 50 participants.
